title: Indonesia, the largest
hookLine: the country with the most Muslims in the world

lines: WHERE DO THE MOST MUSLIMS LIVE?
NOT WHERE THE FIRST GUESS LANDS.
cards: Quick question. Where do the most Muslims on earth live? Not, by the usual count, in the lands of Arabic street signs.

Go far to the east, across an ocean, to a country of islands, volcanoes and rice terraces, where the street signs are in the Latin alphabet and the call to prayer drifts over palm trees and motorbikes.
Java, where the nine saints taught, is one of its islands. Today: Indonesia.

teach.b: Indonesia is usually counted as the country with the largest Muslim population in the world.
And inside that line is a surprise: the faith that arrived with traders and teachers didn't erase the islands' languages. It learned them.
Indonesians speak many languages at home and share one national language, Bahasa Indonesia, written in Latin letters.
The prayers are in Arabic, the sermons often in Indonesian, and the songs may be in Javanese or Sundanese or another island tongue.

teach.h: THE DIFFERENCE OF YOUR LANGUAGES: A SIGN.
teach.b: The Qur'an has a line for that: "And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours." In that verse, differences of language aren't a problem to be solved.
They're signs. Indonesia also holds its Muslims alongside neighbors of other faiths: Christians, Hindus in Bali, Buddhists, Confucians.
Its national motto is Old Javanese, Bhinneka Tunggal Ika, usually rendered unity in diversity. Among Muslims there, two well-known movements stand out.
Nahdlatul Ulama tends to keep the older customs: the pesantren, the village boarding school, and visiting the graves of saints.
Muhammadiyah, more of a reform movement, runs schools and hospitals and prefers a plainer practice.
They differ, they argue, and both are deeply Indonesian.
So the number is only the doorway. Inside is a faith that speaks with many island accents.

how: Indonesian Muslims pray in Arabic, often hear the Friday sermon in Indonesian or a local language, and students may study in pesantren or schools run by movements such as Nahdlatul Ulama and Muhammadiyah.

o: an Arabic-speaking country at the center of the Muslim world
an island nation usually counted as home to the most Muslims
a single island where the nine saints of Java taught

s: the country with the most Muslims is in the Middle East
Indonesia, far to the east, is usually counted as the largest.
Bahasa Indonesia is written in Arabic letters
it is written in Latin letters. the prayers are in Arabic.
the Qur'an calls the difference of languages a sign
Qur'an 30:22 counts the difference of your languages among His signs.

games.q: you're a teacher in an Indonesian village. your listeners speak Javanese at home, Indonesian at school and pray in Arabic. what language is the sermon in?
o: often Indonesian or the local language.
games.why: the prayers stay in Arabic, but the sermon is often given in Indonesian or a local language so people can follow it.

practice: Here's an Indonesian word: terima kasih, thank you. Say it slowly, teh-REE-mah KAH-see, once on each out-breath, and give it in your head to three people you'd like to thank.
If you pray, you can thank God in whatever language you pray in; if not, let the thanks land on the people.

wordCard.voice: Indonesia. The island nation usually counted as home to more Muslims than any other, where one faith speaks in many languages. Today's word.
